summary: SEC charged 18 defendants in a $300M international pump-and-dump scheme involving microcap stocks. Promoters used social media and newsletters to inflate prices of shell companies with no real operations.
notes: Largest pump-and-dump case of 2024. Key lesson: social media promotion + no revenue = red flag.

summary: SEC halted trading in 15 microcap stocks promoted through coordinated Twitter and Discord campaigns. Promoters dumped shares after creating artificial demand.
notes: Social media coordination is the #1 pump signal. Multiple platforms = higher confidence.

summary: Canadian Securities Administrators warned about social media pump-and-dump schemes targeting Canadian investors. Schemes used WhatsApp groups and Telegram channels to coordinate buying of TSX-V penny stocks.
notes: TSX-V penny stocks are frequent targets. Low liquidity = easier to manipulate.

summary: SEC charged crypto promoter with manipulating two digital assets through coordinated buying and misleading social media posts. Promoter sold holdings after price spike for $2M profit.
notes: Crypto pump-and-dump follows same pattern as stocks. Lower regulation = more fraud.

summary: SEC charged crypto exchange with wash trading to inflate reported volume. Platform executed buy and sell orders without economic substance to appear more active than it was.
notes: Wash trading = volume without ownership change. Hard to detect without order book data. Volume anomaly is key indicator.

summary: CFTC fined a proprietary trading firm $50M for wash trading in commodity futures. Firm executed pre-arranged trades with no market risk to manipulate settlement prices.
notes: Futures wash trading is high-priority CFTC enforcement area.

summary: DOJ convicted trader for spoofing gold and silver futures. Trader placed large orders he never intended to execute, then cancelled them after the market moved.
notes: Spoofing requires order book data to detect. This system cannot detect spoofing directly — flag unusual spread patterns.

summary: CFTC imposed $1B penalty (largest ever) on commodity trader for widespread spoofing across precious metals and Treasury futures over 8 years.
notes: Spoofing at scale = billions in penalties. Flag any ticker with unusual spread + volume pattern.

summary: SEC charged 5 corporate executives with insider trading ahead of merger announcements. Executives used family accounts to hide trades.
notes: Unusual volume before a major announcement is the #1 insider trading red flag.

summary: Ontario Securities Commission banned a mining executive for insider trading. Executive bought shares before positive drill results were made public.
notes: Mining sector is high-risk for insider trading due to information asymmetry around exploration results.

summary: SEC charged short-seller research firm for publishing false negative reports to drive down stock prices, then covering short positions at a profit.
notes: Short & distort is the inverse of pump & dump. Same mechanics, opposite direction.

summary: FINRA fined broker $2M for excessive trading (churning) in client accounts. Broker executed trades solely to generate commissions with no benefit to client.
notes: Churning = excessive trading for commissions. Not detectable from market data alone.

summary: SEC charged broker-dealer with front-running customer orders. Trader executed personal trades ahead of large customer orders to profit from the price movement.
notes: Front running = trading ahead of customer orders. Illegal. Flag if a broker seems to consistently trade ahead of you.

summary: SEC suspended trading in 28 penny stocks promoted through 'investment newsletters' that were actually paid advertisements. Companies paid promoters in shares, promoters dumped on retail.
notes: Paid newsletters = pump. Never trust 'free' stock tips in newsletters.

summary: Australian Securities and Investments Commission charged 4 individuals with pump-and-dump via Telegram group. Group leader bought microcap, hyped to followers, dumped at profit.
notes: Telegram groups are the #1 platform for coordinated pumps globally.

summary: SEC charged celebrity influencers for promoting crypto tokens without disclosing they were paid. Tokens crashed 90%+ after promotion ended.
notes: Celebrity crypto promotion = 99% scam. Never buy based on influencer hype.

summary: SEC shut down $1.7B crypto Ponzi scheme. Platform promised 10% monthly returns from 'algorithmic trading' but was paying old investors with new investors' money.
notes: Guaranteed returns = Ponzi. If it sounds too good to be true, it is.

summary: SEC charged trader with 'marking the close' — executing large trades at market close to manipulate closing price and benefit derivative positions.
notes: Marking the close = manipulating closing price. Flag large orders in last 5 minutes of trading.

summary: UK Financial Conduct Authority fined investment banker for insider trading. Banker traded on confidential M&A information obtained through his role.
notes: M&A context + unusual volume = high probability insider trading. Flag any unusual pre-announcement activity.

summary: SEC halted stock promoted through 'free stock pick' websites that were fronts for offshore boiler rooms. Retail investors lost over $10M.
notes: Free stock picks from unknown websites = pump. Never trust unsolicited recommendations.

summary: CSA warned about 'COVID-recovery' themed pump-and-dump schemes. Promoters used pandemic narrative to promote worthless small caps.
notes: Theme-based pumps follow news cycles. Whatever is trending = pump target.

summary: Volume abnormality: daily volume exceeds 500% of 20-day average with no accompanying news or SEC filing. High probability of wash trading or coordinated activity.
Circular ownership pattern: same entity buying and selling through multiple accounts. Creates illusion of market activity without real economic transfer.
Volume-to-market-cap ratio exceeds 100% consistently. Stock trading more than its total market cap daily is likely being washed.
